answer: The river multiplier is published, charged in hollow, and onyx lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1907 identities would post 2809 proofs and burn roughly 71 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
